text:
jordan_pm: Heads-up — product asked to prioritize a routing policy "fabric" roadmap doc. customer asks: region pinning + tenant-level isolation for regulated customers. need to align phasing and launch criteria.

maria_eng: +1. propose 3 phases: 0) policy tags + affinity hints, 1) centralized policy engine + eval paths, 2) hard tenant slices with capacity isolation.

sam_arch: Phase boundaries look good. question: do we treat region pinning as a policy or a capability of slot allocation? has perf implications.

maria_eng: Region pinning should live in policy layer but enforce via scheduler knobs. cheap option first: add routing tag "region_hint" to requests, fallback to soft steering.

kai_infra: FYI, hard slices require accounting changes + reservation slots on dedicated pools. rough infra work: quota changes, metrics per-slice, migration tooling. estimate 6 wks for minimal infra to support soft steering + observability.

cs-lee: Customer (FinBank) will accept soft steering for initial pilot if we guarantee data residency guards and audit logs. they asked for SLA for failover windows.

jordan_pm: Important. So launch criteria for pilot = soft steering + residency audit + runbook for failover. Full GA requires per-tenant isolation + SLOs.

maria_eng: Drafted a tiny config prototype to discuss:
```
routing_policy:
  phases: [soft_hint, policy_engine, tenant_slices]
  soft_hint:
    region_hint: user.region
    fallback: nearest-available
```
Keep this lightweight so customers can opt-in.

sam_arch: Concern — soft_hint still requires KV cache routing awareness. without cache-aware routing we'll see token-level latency spikes on cross-region hits. Need benchmark.

kai_infra: Agree. propose experimental benchmark pool: 2 nodes in eu-west + 2 in us-west, run synthetic with region_hint toggled. I'll spin up a canary.

jordan_pm: Budget and priority question: where does this sit vs. autoscaling revamp? Product wants routing prioritized because it unlocks more enterprise deals.

maria_eng: From eng POV, routing + observability is higher ROI for sales. autoscaling revamp can be decoupled; we can ship phase0 without it.

cs-lee: Sales note — having a clear phased contract clause helps. customers want dates + migration support.

sam_arch: Minimum viable rollout checklist suggestion:
- pilot docs + runbook
- residency audit + KMS confirmation
- bench: cross-region latency < X ms for 95% after soft steering
- migration tool for tenant move (dry-run mode)
- cost estimate delta to customer

kai_infra: Add infra gating: per-tenant metrics emitted, quota enforcement tested, and fallback policy tested under load.

jordan_pm: Great. Next steps: kai to run bench + infra feasibility by EOW, maria to turn config prototype into PR draft, sam to prepare checklist for arch review. I'll consolidate into a product RFC after those items.

ops-bot: deploy-notice: canary pool created (canary-routing-test-2026) by kai_infra at 2759876575 :rocket:

maria_eng: noted — I'll start the RFC outline now. tagging @cs-lee for customer-facing commit language. :eyes:

cs-lee: will prep customer communication template and contract clause sample.

jordan_pm: Thanks team. keeping this thread as the single source for routing policy fabric phasing. will update with links once RFC is up. :thumbsup:
